chunks: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim to build the Kaaba and to raise its foundations and show the people their rituals. So Ibrahim and Ismail built the House every day, course by course, until they reached the place of the Black Stone.

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Then Mount Abu Qubays called out to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'There is a trust with me for you!' So it gave him the Stone, and he placed it in its place. Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) called out among the people for the Hajj and said: 'O people! I am Ibrahim, the Friend of God! God commands you to perform the Hajj of this House, so perform its Hajj!' So those who would perform Hajj until the Day of Resurrection answered him, and the first to answer him were from the people of Yemen.

He said: And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) performed the Hajj — he himself, his family, and his children. So whoever claims that the one to be slaughtered was Ishaq — it would have been from this very place he was slaughtered.
And it is mentioned from Abu Basir that he heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) both claiming that it was Ishaq, while Zurara claimed that it was Ismail.

key_terms.أبو قبيس: Mount Abu Qubays — a mountain adjacent to Mecca, believed in Islamic tradition to have been a repository for the Black Stone
key_terms.الحجر الأسود: The Black Stone — a sacred stone embedded in the eastern corner of the Kaaba, said to have descended from Paradise
key_terms.الذبيح: The one to be slaughtered — the son whom Ibrahim (AS) was commanded to sacrifice; the identity (Ismail or Ishaq) is a matter of scholarly debate
key_terms.الكعبة: The Kaaba — the cubic structure at the center of al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, the holiest site in Islam
key_terms.خليل الله: Friend of God (Khalilullah) — a title of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), from Quran 4:125

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kafi narrate about Ibrahim and Ismail building the Kaaba and the Black Stone?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the divine command to Prophet Ibrahim (AS) to build the Kaaba and establish the rites of Hajj. The narrative includes the miraculous retrieval of the Black Stone from Mount Abu Qubays, Ibrahim's proclamation calling humanity to pilgrimage — a call that reverberates through all time — and his personal performance of Hajj. It concludes with a scholarly discussion among early Shia authorities about the identity of the 'Dhabih' (the one offered for sacrifice) — with Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq reportedly claiming it was Ishaq, while Zurara reported it was Ismail, reflecting an ongoing theological debate.
